source.title: Claude Cowork Now Runs Any LLM. Test It Free.
source.author: Paweł Huryn

athena.directive: The Creative Liberation Engine shall embody ultimate sovereignty and adaptability in the LLM ecosystem, empowering users and enterprises with complete control over their AI infrastructure, models, and data, while delivering unparalleled agentic capabilities.
athena.rationale: The quiet release by Anthropic, allowing Claude Cowork to run any LLM, signals a critical shift towards LLM agnosticism and user control. This validates the Creative Liberation Engine's core constitutional principle of sovereignty (Article I) and presents a strategic opportunity to leapfrog competitors by building a truly open, self-owned, and highly configurable agentic platform that is not beholden to any single model provider. The focus on enterprise-grade controls and data residency also aligns with our quality standards (Article IV) and commitment to complete solutions (Article IX).

options.title: Creative Liberation Engine: The Universal Agentic Operating System
options.description: Develop the Creative Liberation Engine as a comprehensive operating system for agentic AI, capable of orchestrating any LLM (local, open-source, commercial via gateways) and providing a highly customizable, self-hosted environment for building and deploying advanced agents. This includes native support for enterprise compliance, data residency, and a rich ecosystem of self-managed tools and skills.
options.tradeoffs: High development complexity and time investment. Requires significant engineering resources to build out a robust, production-grade OS. May initially struggle with broad adoption compared to existing platforms.

options.title: Adaptive LLM Gateway & Orchestrator for Creative Liberation Engine
options.description: Prioritize building a sophisticated, self-owned LLM gateway within the Creative Liberation Engine. This gateway would abstract away the complexities of integrating with various LLMs (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex, local models via LiteLLM/Ollama proxies), providing a unified API for agents and applications, complete with fine-grained access control, cost management, and intelligent model routing based on task requirements and compliance needs.
options.tradeoffs: Still requires significant integration effort for each new LLM/provider. Might become a maintenance burden if not designed with extreme extensibility. Less direct control over the 'workspace' aspect compared to a full OS.

options.title: Creative Liberation Engine Enterprise: Compliance-First Agent Platform
options.description: Focus exclusively on the enterprise market, designing the Creative Liberation Engine from the ground up with a 'compliance-first' mentality. This means deep integration with enterprise cloud providers (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure AI Foundry), advanced data residency controls, robust audit trails (OpenTelemetry), and comprehensive admin capabilities (token caps, MCP allowlisting). The agentic framework would be optimized for highly regulated workflows.
options.tradeoffs: Niche market focus, potentially limiting broader adoption. Higher barrier to entry for individual developers or smaller teams. May require extensive legal and compliance expertise during development.

options.title: Open-Source Agent Workbench with Decentralized Tools
options.description: Create an open-source 'agent workbench' that enables users to easily configure and deploy agents using their preferred LLMs and a decentralized ecosystem of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for tools. This option emphasizes community contributions for tools and skills, similar to how MCP servers are being developed. It would prioritize ease of customization and extensibility for developers.
options.tradeoffs: Reliance on community for tool development might lead to inconsistent quality or lack of critical integrations. Monetization strategy could be less clear. Requires a strong community management effort.

options.title: CLE Core: A Minimalist, High-Performance Agent Runtime
options.description: Develop a highly optimized, minimalist agent runtime within the Creative Liberation Engine. This core would focus solely on efficient agent execution and LLM interaction, offloading complex UI, admin, and tool management to external, pluggable modules or existing third-party solutions. The goal is maximum performance and flexibility, allowing users to 'bring their own' everything else.
options.tradeoffs: May feel incomplete or require significant setup for end-users without a rich UI or built-in features. Risks becoming a 'building block' rather than a complete product.

options.title: AI-Powered 'Skill & Plugin Fabric' for Cross-Platform Agents
options.description: Focus on building a universal 'skill and plugin fabric' that allows agents in the Creative Liberation Engine to dynamically discover, integrate, and utilize tools and capabilities across any LLM or platform. This would involve developing a semantic understanding layer that can translate agent requests into tool calls, regardless of the underlying LLM's specific tool-calling syntax, effectively solving the manual import and flakiness issues.
options.tradeoffs: Highly theoretical and technically challenging. Requires significant research and development into agentic tool use and semantic parsing. Might take a long time to mature.
